question.prompt: Mr. and Mrs. Zeta want to name their baby Zeta so that its monogram (first, middle, and last initials) will be in alphabetical order with no letters repeated. How many such monograms are possible?

solutions.explanation:
The last initial is fixed as \(Z\), so the first and middle initials must be two different letters from \(A\) through \(Y\). Once those two letters are chosen, alphabetical order uniquely determines which comes first and which comes second.

There are \(25\cdot24\) ways to select two distinct letters in order. Each pair is counted twice, once in each selection order, so the number of pairs is
\[
\frac{25\cdot24}{2}=\boxed{300}.
\]
Every pair produces one valid monogram by putting its letters in alphabetical order and appending \(Z\), and every valid monogram arises from exactly one pair. Thus the answer is choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
solutions.title: Choose the two initials before Z
